title: Molina breaks through for first DTM win
dek: Miguel Molina converted pole into his first DTM win, 7.500 seconds ahead of Paul di Resta, while Pascal Wehrlein's fifth place stretched his title lead to 37 points.

chapters.title: Saturday's win for Martin leaves Wehrlein 27 clear
text: Saturday had belonged to Maxime Martin, whose BMW won the red-flagged first race from Edoardo Mortara and Pascal Wehrlein. Wehrlein's third place stretched his championship lead to 27 points: he led on 155, with Mortara on 128 and Mattias Ekström on 127. Sunday's race would run for an hour with a compulsory pit stop, and with 75 points left a win for Wehrlein combined with a poor day for his two Audi rivals could have ended the title fight before the Hockenheim finale.

chapters.title: Molina on pole, the title rivals out of position
text: Miguel Molina took pole with a lap of 1m21.732s, 0.207s clear of Tom Blomqvist's BMW, a day after a first-lap crash had ended his Saturday race. Jamie Green was third, Paul di Resta fourth and Bruno Spengler fifth, ahead of Augusto Farfus, Robert Wickens and Maximilian Götz, with Wehrlein ninth and Marco Wittmann tenth.

The three men fighting for the title fared far worse. Wehrlein, ninth on 1m22.219s, was in the heaviest car in the field and with only one fresh set of tyres left after starting Saturday's race on new ones. Ekström qualified 17th and Mortara 20th. Martin, Saturday's winner, was 16th, Lucas Auer, Saturday's pole-sitter, 15th. Gary Paffett did not set a time, because his Mercedes had suffered an engine failure in the warm-up and the replacement unit was not ready in time. Martin Tomczyk did set a time, but he was sent to the back of the grid with a penalty for work on his sealed engine.

chapters.title: Green stalls and the safety car appears
text: Molina got away cleanly and held off Blomqvist into Turn 1, but Green, starting third, could not get his Audi moving. He dropped to the back and would end the day 17th, which ended his title hopes. At the first corner Wickens and Scheider collided, leaving Scheider's Audi stuck in the gravel, and the safety car was deployed.

After the restart Molina quickly pulled clear. Blomqvist, who had led the chase early on, was passed by di Resta and Spengler and ended up a lonely fourth. Paffett was turned around at Turn 4 by Marco Wittmann's BMW early on, and his race ended after eight laps with engine trouble, despite a new unit having been fitted after the morning failure.

chapters.title: Slow stops hurt Wehrlein and Ekström
text: When the pit window opened and the cars came in for their compulsory stops, two of the title contenders lost time. Wehrlein and Ekström each had a slow stop at the front-left wheel. Wehrlein dropped three places, to Götz, Juncadella and Farfus, complained furiously over the radio, and was also held briefly to avoid an unsafe release. Ekström's stop dropped him out of the top ten and he never made it back into the points, finishing 11th.

Wehrlein repaired some of the damage with a forceful pass on Farfus around the outside of the chicane. Rockenfeller was among the last to stop, around half distance, and came out behind Wehrlein, immediately pressing the Mercedes.

chapters.title: Mortara and Glock collide, and Mercedes help Wehrlein
text: After 28 laps Mortara, who needed points to stay in the title picture, tangled with Timo Glock in a pack fighting for places. The two made contact at Turn 3, and Mortara spun, rolled backwards towards the tyre stack and parked. The stewards gave Glock a drive-through and Mortara a warning.
Meanwhile Mercedes team-mates helped Wehrlein. Daniel Juncadella dropped in behind him and held up Rockenfeller, and Götz slowed on one lap to let the championship leader by into fifth place.

chapters.title: Molina wins by 7.5 seconds
text: Molina crossed the line after 43 laps in 1h02m00.166s, 7.500s ahead of di Resta, who had closed up after the stops before the Audi pulled away again. Spengler took third, 8.791s down, so for the second day running all three manufacturers were on the podium. Blomqvist was fourth, Wehrlein fifth, Götz sixth, Mike Rockenfeller seventh and Farfus eighth.

Tomczyk, from the back of the grid, made it to ninth and Juncadella scored the final point in tenth. Molina also set the fastest lap, a 1m23.417s on lap 16. It was his first DTM win and made him the 12th different winner of the 2015 season.

chapters.title: Wehrlein nearly there as Audi and Mercedes trade barbs
text: Molina said he had made a clean getaway at the start and again at the restart, and that the day had been without mistakes; the last ten laps, he added, were the longest he had ever driven. He had started from pole before without winning. Di Resta said that after his mistake in Saturday qualifying everything had been better on Sunday, and that he had come close after the stops before Molina pulled away. Spengler, whose BMW had been badly damaged on Saturday, said he had a great car but could not catch di Resta, and that Molina was in a different league.

The mood in the Audi camp was soured by Mercedes' tactics. Audi's DTM head Dieter Gass said the manufacturers had agreed to keep the racing clean and that two had kept to it and one had not, pointing to the lap times of Juncadella and Götz. Mercedes' Ulrich Fritz replied that the team saw itself as a team and went for the best possible result, and that it had not acted unsportingly at any point in the race. BMW's motorsport director Jens Marquardt, by contrast, said his team had turned a difficult weekend into a success, with a race win to its name and a driver still in the title fight.

It was a miserable Sunday for Audi's title candidates. Mortara was out after the clash with Glock, and Ekström, who said the car had simply not been quick enough on either day, was also fined 1,000 euros because the pit-stop signal light on his car had not been switched on. After Green's 17th place, even 50 points from the last two races could not take him past Wehrlein.

Wehrlein now led on 165 points, 37 ahead of Mortara on 128 and 38 ahead of Ekström on 127, with Spengler fourth on 119, Green fifth on 107 and Wittmann sixth on 104. Fourteen points at Hockenheim would be enough to secure the title regardless of what the others did, and only Mortara, Ekström and Spengler could still catch him. Wehrlein himself was cautious: 50 points were left, he said, and a lot could happen, but unless things went badly wrong it looked good. The finale takes place on 17 and 18 October, with two races at the Hockenheimring.

facts.v: Miguel Molina won over 43 laps in 1h02m00.166s, 7.500s ahead of Paul di Resta, and became the season's 12th different winner.
